name: Teams
description: Teams: named groups of agents you can address as one. Governance shell over the in-crate teams store (agent-id membership only); no documents, no external dependencies. Runs the out-of-process ryu-teams sidecar; Core proxies /api/teams/* to it.
tagline: Address a group of agents as one

permission_levels.label: Can view
permission_levels.description: See agent teams and which agents belong to each.

permission_levels.label: Can manage
permission_levels.description: Create teams and change their membership, which decides which agents answer when a team is addressed as one.

hook_events.title: Team created
hook_events.description: A new team was persisted, from the desktop, the API, or Core's own agent-builder. Fires exactly once per team, on the insert that mints its id — a failed create does not fire. The payload is the team record as `GET /api/teams/{id}` returns it, so a brand-new team may already carry members (they can be supplied at create time) and its `coordination` defaults to `broadcast`.

hook_events.title: Team changed
hook_events.description: A team's configuration changed — renamed, re-described, its coordination strategy or lead agent swapped, or an agent added to / removed from its roster. Fires for BOTH the full patch (`PATCH /api/teams/{id}`) and the incremental member endpoints the desktop's drag-an-agent-into-a-team gesture uses, so "when an agent joins a team" never misses a path. Both member endpoints are idempotent, and a re-add of an existing member (or a remove of one who was never on the team) changes nothing and does not fire. The payload is the team AFTER the change, not a diff; compare `members` against your own last-seen copy to see who moved.

hook_events.title: Team deleted
hook_events.description: A team was removed. Fires only when a row was actually deleted, so deleting an id that does not exist is silent. The payload is the team as it stood immediately BEFORE the delete — captured then because nothing can look it up afterwards — which is what lets a consumer clean up per-team or per-member state it was holding.
